blocks.name: Classifying oxides
blocks.definition: Classify oxides as acidic, including SO2 and CO2, or basic, including CuO and CaO, related to metallic and non-metallic character

blocks.text: Classifying oxides as acidic or basic

blocks.md:
- Oxides are compounds made from one or more atoms of oxygen combined with one other element
- Examples of oxides include:

  - Magnesium oxide - MgO
  - Zinc oxide - ZnO
  - Potassium oxide - K<sub>2</sub>O
  - Carbon dioxide - CO<sub>2</sub>
  - Sulfur dioxide - SO<sub>2</sub>
  - Water - H<sub>2</sub>O
- Oxides can be classified based on their acid-base characteristics

- Acidic oxides are formed when a **non-metal** element combines with oxygen
- Common examples include:

  - CO<sub>2</sub>
  - SO<sub>2</sub>
  - NO<sub>2</sub>
  - SiO<sub>2</sub>

- Basic oxides are formed when a **metal** element combines with oxygen
- Common examples include:

  - CuO
  - CaO

blocks.md: ***Metals form basic oxides while non-metals form acidic oxides***
